items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: we had a singer named Anita Derian

ctx.x: It was misleading and unfair to the people who bought the band, but we did it because we were forced to do it. We were even kicked out of the union for a while for debt.

So Sperry, in the Army, --we had a singer named Anita Derian who was the girlfriend of a German who had come here as a kid, he became an American citizen, served in the Army and all that, whose mother was an actress in Germany before the war. They had run ahead of the Nazis all the way through--the Jewish people--and wound up in Turkey where they managed to survive somehow through the war, and at the end of it was one of those exchange kids. They rought them here because they weren't eating over there.

So around '55 or so, I think the mother got him a position in Sutgart in radio as a producer and went back there and there met Sperry. Now meanwhile, we have this girl singer and Sperry in our band and they struck up a thing and as it turns out, those radio stations each had a house group--
